# Deck project notes

Planning notes for the back deck, 12 by 14 feet, about 40 inches above the lawn.

## Planning and footings

Our frost depth is 36 inches, so each footing must go at least 36 inches deep to sit below the frost line. Dig 12-inch-diameter holes, pour concrete with a post anchor set in the wet concrete, and let it cure for 48 hours before loading it. Footings on soil that heaves in winter will lift the deck.

## Joist spans

Tables for No. 2 southern pine joists at 16 inches on center: a 2x6 spans up to 9 ft 9 in, a 2x8 spans up to 12 ft 4 in, and a 2x10 spans up to 15 ft 8 in. At 24 inches on center subtract about two feet. A span is the distance between supports, not the length of the board. Add a mid-span blocking row for spans over 8 feet.

## Beam spans and post spacing

A built-up beam of two 2x10s can carry joists out to 8 feet between posts; three 2x10s or two 2x12s go to 10 feet. Set the posts on the footings and notch the beam into them with through-bolts, never relying on nails.

## Ledger board

The ledger attaches the deck to the house and carries about half its load. Remove the siding, fasten the ledger to the rim joist with 1/2-inch lag screws or through-bolts staggered every 16 inches, and flash it above and behind. A ledger fastened with nails alone is the most common reason a deck pulls away from the house.

## Decking boards

Leave a gap of 1/8 to 1/4 inch between boards for drainage and expansion. Fasten each board with two deck screws at every joist. Use stainless or coated screws with treated lumber.

## Railings

A guardrail 36 inches high is required where the deck is more than 30 inches above grade. Balusters must be spaced so a 4-inch sphere cannot pass through. Posts must be bolted to the framing, not just the decking.

## Permit and inspection

A deck more than 30 inches above grade or attached to the house needs a building permit. The inspector looks at the footing holes before the concrete is poured, at the framing, and at the finished railings.
